title: Simplified Motion: Net Force and Acceleration in One Direction
learningObjectives: Explain that simplified one-dimensional motion keeps one pair of opposing forces balanced while the net force in the chosen direction determines motion.
Describe how balanced forces give zero net force and constant velocity and unbalanced forces give a change in motion.
Calculate acceleration as net force divided by mass and predict the direction of acceleration from the sign of the net force.

explanations.text: Simplified motion isolates a single direction and examines one net force at a time, with other forces held in balance, allowing acceleration along that line to be found from F = m * a.

evidence.quote: This page shows some rules for the simplified motion of an aircraft.

explanations.text: Level flight at constant speed represents balanced forces where net force is zero, so acceleration is zero and velocity does not change.

evidence.quote: In an ideal situation, an airplane could sustain a constant speed and level flight
The net force is the difference between the opposing forces; lift minus weight, or thrust minus drag.

explanations.text: When opposing forces become unbalanced the aircraft moves in the direction of the greater force, and the amount of acceleration equals net force divided by mass.

evidence.quote: If the forces become unbalanced, the aircraft will move in the direction of the greater force.
